newsitem.title: UK: No change in British policy on EMU - ministers.
newsitem.headline: No change in British policy on EMU - ministers.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind and Finance Minister Kenneth Clarke on Thursday denied any differences over Britain's approach to a single European currency.
Government policy had not changed, they said in a statement.
"We are hostile to the notion that a single currency can proceed at any stage on a non-convergent basis," they said in response to a Reuters query.
"Government policy has not changed," they added.

The joint statement followed an apparent rift between the two men after Rifkind said Britain was "on balance hostile" to joining a European single currency, due to take effect on January 1, 1999. Clarke said Rifkind had made "a slip of the tongue" but the foreign secretary denied this. The government had established an uneasy truce on European Monetary Union (EMU) at a cabinet meeting on January 23 when it declared that while Britain would keep its options open, it was unlikely to join up if the currency went ahead as planned in 1999.
The two men said on Thursday they remained committed to the statement made after that cabinet meeting.
